requests.purpose: initial composite; warrior was too large
requests.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: one pixel-art visual proposal for intoDeDung, warrior placed on the game's current grass tiles.
Input images: image1 is the exact clean transparent Defender to preserve as the character identity/pose/art; image2 is the existing grass tile texture and shape; image3 is the actual current battle screenshot, use it only for the accepted subdued olive ground palette, projection and character-to-cell proportions, do not copy its interface or other units.
Primary request: place the SAME warrior from image1 on the middle tile of a small contiguous 3-by-3 diamond grid made from the grass tiles. This is a close presentation of how the new warrior drawing looks on the new tiles, not a character redesign.
Composition: a single centered nine-tile patch floating against the plain deep navy background of the game, all nine tile tops visible, small margin around the patch, one and only one warrior on the central cell. Enlarge the whole composition together for viewing while maintaining the existing small relative warrior size. Each tile top diamond has width:height ratio 4:3 (128 by96 game units), not a shallow2:1 isometric tile. Character visible height is only about57.6 game units versus96 for ONE tile's vertical diagonal (60 percent of that diagonal); character visible width about62 game units versus128 tile width. Never enlarge him into a giant spanning several cells. His boots meet the middle tile slightly below its center, his helmet extends upward. Keep body and both feet naturally grounded on the same plane. Do not center the sprite bounding box on the tile center.
Character invariants: reuse the reference silhouette and clean pixel clusters as faithfully as possible: silver rounded helmet, visible warm face, big silver shoulder plates, olive tabard and plain olive shield on viewer-right, sword pointing lower-left, brown boots, bent separated legs, same ready pose and elevated three-quarter view. Keep hands, face and sword individually readable; do not introduce mushy detail, extra ornaments or new equipment.
Ground: use the grass tile material and simple sparse tufts from image2 but the darker restrained olive color balance of image3: midtones around RGB85,92,57, cooler dark olive shadows, muted brown worn patches. Quiet seams between the nine cells. Retain some quiet open ground under the warrior, no grass hiding his boots. A thin dark olive earth edge along the outer front perimeter only, no thick floating cubes and no gaps between cells.
Lighting and medium: same restrained neutral daylight as the references. Coherent pixel-art clusters, clean stepped contours, no painted blur. Preserve existing character highlights. No dramatic new directional lighting, long cast shadows, glow, bloom or atmospheric effects. At most a tiny unobtrusive contact darkening at the boots.
No HUD, no labels, no lettering, no health bars, no selection outlines, no additional units, no traps, no props, no inset panels, no arrows, no watermark. One clear cohesive illustration.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this provided pixel-art warrior-on-nine-grass-tiles illustration. Make exactly one correction: reduce ONLY the warrior's whole visible silhouette to 67 percent of its current linear width and height. He is currently too large relative to a tile. His final helmet-to-lowest-boot height should be about194 pixels on this same1448x1086 canvas, instead of the current approximately290 pixels. Scale sword, shield, helmet, armor, both feet together by this same factor, keep the same crisp pixel art and pose and material colors. Anchor the scaling about the midpoint between the two boot soles near image location(730,584), so the character continues to stand at the same place in the central tile; do not center his bounding box on the cell. Shrink the tiny contact shadow to match; fill exposed ground with matching olive grass. Preserve the entire tile grid, all grass tufts, seams, earth patches, outer edges, camera, composition, navy background, canvas size and lighting. Do not change the warrior design or recolor him. Do not zoom the camera or enlarge the tiles. No other changes, no text, no overlays. The visibly smaller warrior is the required correction.

limitations: Generative placement, tile projection and colors are approximate. Current game geometry is unchanged.
